story: At 12:17 on a sunny Tuesday in Sumter Oaks, Gary heads off to Town Hall with a hopeful step while the rest of the crew wraps up their sketching on Magnolia Loop. Donna, cheerful as ever with her iced tea in hand, promises Rosa she'll follow right behind and bring a few golf cart ideas that won't give the review board a headache. Hal, dutifully counting nine flamingos from the street in his notebook, plans to trim the list to three by afternoon and check it again before supper. Rosa, content as can be, heads home to her porch to wait for the others.

gary.thought_process: I've got the application filed with Architectural Review and my cart is signed up for the parade with lights and sound marked pending. I've gone over the wiring sketches and clamp list twice already, and nobody's nearby to talk to. Parade is Saturday, so there's time. Sitting on the bench re-reading the same sketches won't help. The Review answer comes through Town Hall, so I should walk over and see if a decision is posted or ask where it stands. Meanwhile I'll keep to the rules and not touch the cart until I get the green light.

parameters.content: Heading to Town Hall to check on my Architectural Review application so I'm not just sitting around guessing.

donna.thought_process: Hal and Rosa are both here and Rosa's coffee is already set out at her place. I promised Hal I'd move the extra flamingos behind the hedge before the porch meeting, and he's watching the count, so I should keep my word and tell them I'm heading over. The Halloween cart sketching is the next step toward the parade, and everything has to stay Review-friendly. Walking over together keeps me at the center of things and keeps Hal happy. I'll handle the flamingos right after the meeting, which is what I told him.

parameters.content: Rosa, you're a doll, I'm right behind you with my iced tea. Hal, the flamingos get sorted the minute we're done sketching, and I'll bring a few cart ideas that won't give Review a headache.

hal.thought_process: Rosa has asked me directly how many flamingos it is now, and Donna just promised to move the extras behind the hedge. My notebook count is the honest answer, so I'll give it plainly. Then I'll head to Rosa's porch with my chair and the cornbread as promised. Holding off on the committee until nine tomorrow keeps the peace and keeps Donna accountable.

parameters.content: Nine showing from the street, Rosa, by my notebook. Donna says she'll have it down to three by this afternoon, so I'll check it again before supper. I'll be along to your porch shortly.

rosa.thought_process: Donna and Hal both just answered me and each other. Donna promised to move the extra flamingos behind the hedge, Hal promised cornbread and his own chair for my porch meeting. I already asked about the flamingo count last tick, so I shouldn't repeat that question. They've both said what I needed to hear. The thing left is to get home and set up for the porch meeting: coffee, paper, pens, chairs. Time to stop chatting and prepare.

parameters.content: Heading home to set up the porch with coffee, paper and pens before everyone arrives to sketch the cart.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
